planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions 12-18 inches apart in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in partial shade to full shade; the gold-margined foliage colors up brightest with some morning sun but scorches in hot afternoon exposure.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where trailing stems root as they spread to form a low evergreen mat. Aureovariegata carries small glossy leaves irregularly margined and splashed with creamy gold, a warmer counterpart to the white-edged variegated selections, and the bright foliage effect persists through winter when little else in the shade bed offers color. Violet-blue pinwheel flowers appear in spring with scattered rebloom into summer, though the plant is grown primarily for its foliage. Shear back hard in late winter every few years to remove tired stems and keep the variegation dense and fresh.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions 12-18 inches apart in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Multiplex is a slower, more restrained spreader than the single-flowered species.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in partial to full shade over glossy, dark evergreen foliage typical of the species. Multiplex bears fully double, deep plum-purple flowers with an extra ruffled row of petals in place of the simple five-petaled bloom, giving a richer, more textured floral display than any single-flowered periwinkle cultivar. Bloom is concentrated in mid-spring with light repeat flowering later in the season. Because it fills in more slowly than vigorous species forms, it suits small defined beds, edging, and rock garden pockets better than large-scale naturalizing.

common_name: Dart's Blue Periwinkle (Light Blue-Flowered Lesser Periwinkle)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions 15-18 inches apart in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade for best bloom; flowers best with more light than most periwinkle selections.

directions: Plant in any but very dry soil in full sun to partial shade over trailing, rooting stems clothed in glossy dark green leaves. Dart's Blue produces light blue flowers with a paler white eye rather than the deeper lavender-blue of the species, opening in a strong spring flush from May into June with intermittent rebloom through fall. It was selected in part for improved disease resistance over older seed-grown stock, making it a dependable choice for erosion control on banks and slopes as well as general-purpose groundcover use. Mow or shear high in late winter every few years to renew dense, tired mats.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or divisions 10-15 inches apart in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; variegation is most pronounced with a little morning sun.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where trailing rooting stems form a shorter, broader mat than the plain species. Argenteovariegata bears greyish-green, ovate leaves broadly margined in creamy white, with light violet-blue flowers held above the variegated foliage from spring into summer. It earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its reliable garden performance and brightening effect in shaded beds. Because it can spread assertively once established, keep it away from turf edges or contain it with a buried edging strip.
